opportunities.title: [Bug] Double-submit race: rapid clicks fire duplicate POSTs before isUploading flushes
opportunities.summary: I will pay for a fixed file - details below. ## Bug The guard `disabled={!file || isUploading}` relies on async state flush. Two synchronous activations - fast double-click, Enter+click, assistive-tech activation - dispatch two `handleUpload` invocations while `isUploading` is still `false`, producing duplicate multipart POSTs and racing success/error states. **Repro:** double-click Upload quickly in `Login.tsx`; observe two requests in the network tab. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A synchronous ref-based in-flight guard prevents re-entry regardless of state timing - [ ] Applies to Login.tsx, upload_file.tsx and FileUpload.tsx (or their shared core) - [ ] Regression test asserts handler non-reentrancy ## Reward I will pay **40 USDC (test tokens)** on **ARC Testnet** for a merged fix — same flow as #53, but payout is test USDC on ARC, not Base. How to claim: 1. Comment `/attempt` with this issue number before you start. 2. Open a PR referencing this issue (`Fixes #<this issue>`). 3. After the PR is reviewed and merged, comment your **ARC testnet EVM address** here — you receive 40 test USDC on ARC.

opportunities.summary: `source.md` contains the complete RFC 5322 specification (Internet Message Format). We need a **fully conformant email address parser** in Python that implements the complete ABNF grammar from sections 3.2 through 3.4, plus obsolete syntax from §4.4. opportunities.title: Model fiat currencies and multi-chain token bindings as domain state
opportunities.summary: ## Background The Banking Ledger must distinguish internal fiat-denominated balances from external tokens used for blockchain settlement. An intermediate redesign removed the `Currency` aggregate and introduced a statically injected `SettlementAssetRegistry`. That model has important limitations: - supported currencies and token bindings are queried directly from runtime configuration instead of being reconstructed as Read Models from domain events; - one Currency effectively resolves to only one deposit token and one withdrawal token; - chain identity is hidden behind Solana infrastructure types; and - completed Deposit and Withdrawal aggregates do not retain the blockchain transaction that produced the settlement. Replace the static registry with event-sourced Ledger domain state. Restore `Currency` as a bank-managed aggregate, model multiple token bindings as entities owned by that aggregate, make the supported blockchain explicit in domain values, and project the resulting events into normal Read Models. This does **not** restore the former currency-issuance platform. The bank binds existing external tokens and does not create tokens, publish token metadata, or manage token sup
